Predict size

Source: R/kb_predict_size.R
kb_predict_size.Rd

Predict the expected plant size at each row of new_data, or at the observed data when new_data = NULL.

Usage

kb_predict_size(
  fit,
  new_data = NULL,
  ...,
  new_levels = c("average", "sample"),
  representative_site = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  estimate = stats::median,
  sig_fig = 3
)

Arguments

fit

A kb_fit_size object.

new_data

A data frame with optional site and year columns, one row per prediction, or NULL to predict at the observed data. year may be numeric or character: 2022 and "2022" match the same fitted year.

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

new_levels

A string giving how uncertainty is estimated for a site or year not in the data used to fit the model, or when new_data has no site or year column. Sites and years in the model fit always use their own estimates. One of:

  • "average" (the default): the typical site or year. The site and year effects are set to 0, their mean, so the interval does not include among-site or among-year variation. Use it to describe an average site or year.

  • "sample": a new effect for each new site or year, drawn from the estimated variation among sites or among years (the random-effect standard deviation). The point estimate is equivalent, but the interval is wider since it also includes that variation. Use it to get realistic uncertainty about a particular site or year that the model has no information on. Rows that name the same new site or year, or that have no site or year column, share one effect; give new sites or years different names for independent effects. The interval varies slightly between calls; use set.seed() to reproduce it.

representative_site

A character vector of sites in the fit whose effects a new site adopts (averaged when several are named), or NULL (the default) to follow new_levels.

conf_level

A number greater than 0 and less than 1 giving the compatibility-interval level.

estimate

A function that reduces a numeric vector of posterior draws to a single estimate, such as median or mean.

sig_fig

A whole number of significant figures for summary output.

Value

A kb_predictions object: the rows of new_data with added estimate, lower, and upper columns summarising the posterior distribution of expected size. When the rows have site and year, a size_support column (as in kb_predict_mean_weight()) precedes the summary.

Details

The expected size is the mean of the fitted size distribution (Nereocystis plant diameter in mm).

The size models have no predictor, so new_data needs no columns: each row is a site, a year, or a site-year, given by its optional site and year columns.

With representative_site, a new site also takes the named sites' site:year effect in a year in which they have data.

See also

kb_new_data() to build rows by site or year, and posterior_predict() for draws of individual plant sizes.

Other prediction functions: autoplot.kb_predictions(), kb_new_data(), kb_plot_predictions(), kb_predict_biomass_canopy(), kb_predict_biomass_in_situ(), kb_predict_carbon(), kb_predict_cover_calibration(), kb_predict_mean_weight(), kb_predict_nitrogen(), kb_predict_weight(), kb_predict_wetdry(), predict.kb_fit_carbon(), predict.kb_fit_cover_calibration(), predict.kb_fit_nitrogen(), predict.kb_fit_size(), predict.kb_fit_weight(), predict.kb_fit_wetdry()

Examples

fit <- fit_size_sim_nereo

# At the observed plants:
kb_predict_size(fit)
#> <kb_predictions> response: diameter_mm | by: site, year
#> # A tibble: 900 × 7
#>    diameter_mm site       year  size_support estimate lower upper
#>          <dbl> <fct>      <fct> <chr>           <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1        24.5 otter_cove 2020  site-year          26  23.7  29.2
#>  2        28.3 otter_cove 2020  site-year          26  23.7  29.2
#>  3        30.7 otter_cove 2020  site-year          26  23.7  29.2
#>  4        17.4 otter_cove 2020  site-year          26  23.7  29.2
#>  5        41.7 otter_cove 2020  site-year          26  23.7  29.2
#>  6        18.9 otter_cove 2020  site-year          26  23.7  29.2
#>  7        16.6 otter_cove 2020  site-year          26  23.7  29.2
#>  8        33.5 otter_cove 2020  site-year          26  23.7  29.2
#>  9        32.6 otter_cove 2020  site-year          26  23.7  29.2
#> 10        18.7 otter_cove 2020  site-year          26  23.7  29.2
#> # ℹ 890 more rows

# By site:
kb_predict_size(fit, kb_new_data(fit, by = "site"))
#> <kb_predictions> response: diameter_mm | by: site
#> # A tibble: 9 × 4
#>   site           estimate lower upper
#>   <fct>             <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 otter_cove         25.6  23.3  28  
#> 2 gull_rock          27.5  25    30.3
#> 3 cedar_bay          22.4  20.5  24.8
#> 4 heron_reef         24.4  22.1  26.9
#> 5 urchin_shoal       18.7  16.7  21.3
#> 6 sculpin_head       22.4  20.5  24.6
#> 7 eagle_spit         29.1  26.6  31.9
#> 8 fog_islet          31.8  28.1  36  
#> 9 tidepool_bluff     27.3  25    30.1

# At new rows, including a new site:
kb_predict_size(fit, data.frame(site = c("otter_cove", "new_site")))
#> <kb_predictions> response: diameter_mm | by: site
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   site       estimate lower upper
#>   <chr>         <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 otter_cove     25.6  23.3  28  
#> 2 new_site       25.1  21.4  29.1
